I know this is probably just going to be hypothetical and completely impractical, especially when a stress test was done and SSDs were pretty much proven to last forever under normal conditions, but this thought came to me in the shower:

Considering the fact that you can put different directories in different partitions, and that solid-state drives rely on I/O cycles, would it be "better" to just install the system files to the SSD during the initial install, or install the system to a separate platter-based hard drive, get it "stable" (i.e., not installing a new thing every 15 minutes), then transfer the system partitions to the SSD?

Whenever I install a new Linux, it's usually a brand new system and I go looking for stuff that I either used in the past, or for new tools/toys, so my install is usually "unstable" for the first month or so. Were I to build another computer (I am currently without one), I would like to run Linux as primary OS, but for now, I'm just asking, as I know the practical answer is just to install on the SSD from the start, saving heartache with Grub or rEFIt, but it was a shower thought and I don't actually have the answer.
Kind of an advanced question regarding partitions and SSDs

If the SSD's you've been using are "unstable" I would suggest increasing your budget for storage. I've never heard of installing on a mechanical platter drive and then moving your OS to a SSD for any kind of performance gain, that just sounds like a waste of time.

Thanks, that's pretty much what I thought to be the case, but it was bugging me until I got it out.

Also, what I meant by unstable was crap-ton of writes, ie, the apt-get update && apt-get upgrade && apt-get install new-tool-I-didn_t-know-existed that's bound to occur every day or every other day when I'm getting used to a Debian-based system, for example. This typically has happened for about a month until I got used to the environment I built.

Well, it makes perfect sense to install to platters if you need storage more than OS speediness. My 3rd HDD for my box arrives tomorrow, and I will be glad to have it over the SSD options I looked at. I need to store several TB of data, but don't have any need for super fast SSD load times.

In a year or two when I upgrade again, I may very well choose to get an SSD and install my OS to it, but for now having several more TB of platter space is more important than having faster read/write times.
